headline: Foreign Cyberattacks Hit Academic Blogs, a New Federal Tuition Tax Credit Debuts, and Provosts Say AI Has Outrun Strategy
thesis: A wave of cyberattacks tied to authoritarian regimes hits British academic research blogs the same week Inside Higher Ed finds 7 in 10 provosts use AI weekly while only 1 in 10 institutions have a centralized AI strategy, and a new federal tuition tax credit reshapes school-choice funding.
summary: Inside Higher Ed reports a wave of cyberattacks on British academic blogs that researchers suspect is an effort by authoritarian regimes to shut down work documenting human-rights abuses -- a reminder that campus IT threats extend well beyond ransomware. The warning lands alongside Inside Higher Ed's 2026 survey of chief academic officers, which finds roughly seven in ten provosts now use AI in their own work at least weekly -- mostly to summarize documents and draft communications -- yet only one in ten report their institution has a centralized AI strategy, with staff resistance and capacity gaps cited as the biggest barriers. On the policy side, THE Journal breaks down the new federal Education Freedom Tax Credit, a tax-credit scholarship mechanism its backers say could benefit 90% of students in states that opt in. Workforce readiness is a running thread too: EdTech Digest's Cengage-sourced "Experience Gap" report finds 53% of new graduates have skipped applying to entry-level jobs feeling underqualified, while EdSurge covers how the Reagan Institute's RISE summit and JFF's Maria Flynn are reframing what schools owe students entering an AI-reshaped labor market. Inside K-12 IT shops, EdTech Magazine describes agentic AI taking over routine help-desk tickets and makes the case for "AI bills of materials" to track what automated systems are actually doing, even as its own back-to-school checklist and a fresh EDUCAUSE student-tech report (46% of students hit a security threat last year) underline that the basics still need attention. Fall's conference marathon opens next week, with EDUCAUSE's annual conference starting September 29.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · September 25, 2026 · Items were sourced and dated via web-search indexing rather than live page fetches this run (direct fetches to source sites were blocked by network egress restrictions); Education Technology Insights, 1EdTech, EdTech Week, Ed-Fi and ISTE had no September-dated coverage surface in search, so their most relevant recent items are listed instead with a note.
